hyps.why: Replacing a weak avg_pool on the output edge with a 3x3 conv gives large gains (+3 to +9), whereas replacing a 1x1 conv gives roughly zero.
Swapping a 3x3 conv for a skip on the direct edge was mostly positive, while replacing a 1x1 conv with a skip was often strongly negative.
Replacing an existing skip on edge 3 with a 3x3 conv hurt consistently across all datasets, unlike replacing a 1x1 conv.
Removing edge 0 is much less damaging when a 3x3 conv on edge 1 provides an alternative path.
Removing edge 0 when edge 1 is already none disconnects the cell, causing catastrophic drops.
Upgrading a skip on edge 2 to a 3x3 conv gave consistent gains, while replacing a 1x1 conv gave about zero.
Downgrading a 3x3 conv on the output edge to a skip loses capacity and is mostly harmful across all datasets.
With a weak pooling direct edge, a stronger conv on edge 0 helps on C100 and IN16, while a none direct edge gave clearly negative results.
Upgrading the avg_pool on edge 4 helped consistently when edge 3 is a skip.
The gain from a 3x3 conv on edge 5 was larger with a 1x1 conv on edge 3 than with a skip on edge 3.
